question: What happens to biodegradable substances when they are released in the environment?

options.text: They get broken down into simpler components.
They get converted into toxic chemicals.

solution:
The correct answer is __**They get broken down into simpler components**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Biodegradable substances** are materials that can be broken down or **decomposed** into simpler, harmless substances by the action of **microorganisms** such as **bacteria** and **fungi** over a period of time.
 
• When these substances are released into the environment, biological processes involving **enzymatic actions** convert complex **organic matter** into simpler **inorganic forms** like **carbon dioxide**, **water**, and **minerals**. ***Hence, the statement that they get broken down into simpler components is correct.***
 
• This natural process ensures that nutrients are returned to the **soil** or **atmosphere**, maintaining the **biogeochemical cycles** and the overall **ecological balance** of the planet.
 
• The rate of **decomposition** varies depending on the **nature of the substance** and environmental factors such as **temperature**, **moisture**, and **oxygen availability**.
